   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  NOVEMBER 10, 2022
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  John Vuong, Kim Luu, Katie Chan, Karla Grijalva, Lisa Massaro

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES 9-8-22
  Commission Members will vote to approve 9-8-22 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  UPDATE ITEMS
  a) Sustainability Plan
  b) Tree Ordinance
  c) Turf Replacement Rebate
  d) Recycling Event
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ZERO WASTE EVENTS
  The City of LA is creating zero waste events and zero-waste facilities and every employee will be
  trained on zero waste. They are also banning polystyrene and sales of single-use plastic water
  bottles. Alhambra should encourage refill stores to come to our city and organizations to provide
  these zero waste events.
  Recommended Action: Discussion item. No action required.

  V.  BAN LEAF BLOWERS
  New CA state law bans the sale of gas-powered leaf blowers by the start of 2024. As part of that
  law, $30 million will be made available to sole proprietors and other small landscaping businesses
  to assist in the purchase of zero-emission small off-road equipment, including leaf-blowing
  machines, lawnmowers, and string trimmers. Commission will discuss options for the City of
  Alhambra.
  Recommended Action: Discussion Item. No action required.

  VI.  FRONT YARD OPTION TO REMOVE TURF
  Commission will discuss options available to replace front yard turf for residents in accordance with
  AMC Chapter 23.48.
  Recommended Action: Discussion item. No action required

  VII.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please
  limit all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior
  to the meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business
  of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5)
  minutes.

 VIII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

IX.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, November 10, 2022 at 6:00 p.m.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra

7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact David Dolphin, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting of September 9, 2022

  The regular meeting of the Environmental Committee was called to order at 6:12 p.m.
  on September 9, 2022 through Zoom teleconferencing

  I.  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Vuong, Chan, Massaro

  Commission Members Absent: Luu, Grijalva

  Staff Present:  David Dolphin – Commission Secretary

  Members of the Public

  Craig Cadwallader – Policy Coordinator Surfrider Foundation South Bay

 II.  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES FROM 7/14/22
  Commissioner Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from 7/14/22.
  Commissioner Massaro seconded the motion. All Commissioners present voted in
  favor to approve the minutes. Motion to approve passed.

III.  PLASTIC WASTE REDUCTION REGULATIONS
  Commissioner Chan stated the City already has the Disposable Foodware Items
  regulations in place. Commissioner Chan and other Community members changed it
  to Plastic Waste Reduction Regulations which was copied the City of Los Angeles
  and City of Pasadena. The proposed ordinance was changed to update and add more
  current language. The blue print was added and the black was from existing.
  Commissioner Vuong asked if the regulations were consistent with the City of LA
  and LA County and what are the discrepancies. Commissioner Chan stated the
  discrepancies were pertaining to disposable foodware and clarifying the definition.
  Restaurants are now serving ecofriendly disposable boxes. Commissioner Chan
  would like to encourage to bring their own reusable items to go to these restaurants.
  Also, the restaurants should encourage the limiting of waste as far as take away
  consumption. Commissioner Vuong asked if were there any ambiguities to their
  current legislation. Commissioner Chan responded there are a lot of similarities
  however the City of LA, LA County and Pasadena are more updated in terms of
  purpose of plastic waste reduction and addressing current pollution conditions.
  Commissioner Chan stated the City of Alhambra needs straight to the point
  definitions and readable language in order to be most current. Also, to ensure the
  restaurants in the City will know their responsibility with plastic waste reduction.

  Page 1 of 4
   Commissioners Vuong and Massaro agreed if the changes reflected the current LA
  City and County Plastic Waste Ordinances, Alhambra’s should be updated also. The
  Commission proposed to have this regulation put forth to City Council.
  Commissioner Chan has been in conversation with her City Council Member. Staff
  suggested the Commission to present the ideas to the Council to see if there is enough
  traction to move forward. No other comments have been provided to consider with
  the update of this ordinance.
  Staff identified that a cost would be imposed on the beverage provider and it can be
  negotiable. Commission next steps are to propose to the City Council.

  Staff reminded the Commission that all of the agenda items are available on the
  City’s website.

IV.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN

  The City is waiting for funding through HUD to develop the plan. The funding
  agreement is expected to be approved in Mid-October. The matching grant amount is
  $680K which the City will provide in kind staff time for the match. Staff explained
  the grant process and how the matching funds were obtained. Also, staff told
  Commissioner Chan that once the consultant is chosen, they would have a chance for
  input in order to obtain information for the plan. The Commission decided to add the
  Sustainability Plan update as an agenda update item for the next several meetings.

V.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE UPDATE

  Since February 2019, the City has joined the Clean Power Alliance which purchases
  clean power from renewable sources that is delivered by Southern California Edison
  (SCE). SCE continues to provide billing services and be responsible for resolving any
  issues with electric service. Staff explained the residents can elect to have what
  percentage of electric service provided by green energy; 40%, 50% and 100%.
  The City of Alhambra elected to set the default to 50% for residents. Residents can go
  to the Clean Power Alliance Website if they wish to change the percentage.
  Commissioner Chan asked was this just solar and she was advised by staff that it
  included all renewable energy forms including wind.
  Commissioner Massaro mentioned a flex alert program due to high heat. Public
  comment period was not on agenda but the Commission decided to include the Public
  Comment period as the next item since one hand was raised.

VI.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Craig Callwallader commented. Craig is working with neighboring Cities; Burbank,
  Glendale, Pasadena and Beverly Hills. Craig mentioned he actually wrote the redlines
  listed in our proposed Plastic Waste Regulations and he tracks the plastic waste
  regulations in California, current count 155. The aforementioned cities are working
  on nearly identical ordinances. On Tuesday, the City of Goleta adopted an ordinance
  that was about 95% of what was shown. Neighboring cities would like to keep the
  language similar, that’s why it was suggested for Alhambra. This item was discussed

  Page 2 of 5
   with Council members of the neighboring cities. City of LA does not have their own
  ordinance as of yet. LA County’s ordinance only applies to unincorporated areas.
  Craig worked on ordinances in many cities and would love to answer any questions.
  He also mentioned neighboring cities would like to have similar ordinances. The
  current markup proposal lists blue font as the recommended additions. Craig has been
  working on these regulations for more than a decade, and is willing to provide
  information to the Commission and Council members. It is Craigs hope that all of the
  neighboring cities can adopt the same ordinance so if they were to cross the street to a
  neighboring city the regulations will be similar

  Commissioner Vuong inquired about the 25 cents charge for the reusable items and if
  there are informational materials from different jurisdictions. Craig responded that
  number is based on other ordinances that have been passed like Palm Springs and
  other cities in Northern California which was based on the charge for single use plastic
  bags. The charge was designed as an encouragement to bring reusable items. Also,
  the information will be compiled from several cities and made available to the
  Commission. Craig’s contact information is below:

  Craig Cadwallader - craigc@surfrider-southbay.org, 424-6340452

  Commissioner Vuong has concerns that the information will not get out to the public
  to let them know what the fee is and how to avoid paying if you bring your own
  reusable items. Craig stated public outreach in critical to the success of the ordinance.

VII.  GRANT OPPORTUNITIES

  Commissioner Chan spoke about grants from last meeting. Grants to change the lawn
  to make it more sustainable, i.e., drought tolerant native California plants. LA City
  has something similar, dirt and pebbles and plants. Commissioner Chan would like to
  see the elimination of the policies for mandatory watering of traditional lawns. Staff
  reminded the Commission of the rebates available through SGVMWD and the
  stormwater capture projects the City submitted for funding through the Safe Clean
  Water Program. The Urban greening grant was approved to move forward to the
  second round; inspection scheduled for November 15th. The City has a full-time
  grant specialist and has been successful obtaining grant for our parks. Commissioner
  Chan asked how will Main Street change? The goals of the project include the
  addition of tree canopy and native plants, provide recreation area in the medians and
  remove some concrete areas in order to capture stormwater to increase water supply.

  Massaro likes the idea of drought tolerate landscaping and would like to seek funding
  She thinks this will help to beautify the lawn and save water and at the same time
  help the environment. She is in agreement with pursuing the grant. Commissioner
  Chan mentioned Atwater Village in LA where she viewed some areas which were
  beautiful and grew really well with little water. Most of the landscapes do not have
  green grass and it looks beautiful. The City of LA’s grant is actually a cash for grass
  rebate. Staff informed the Commission that SGVMWD has irrigation and water

  Page 3 of 5
   efficient appliances rebates available but will update at next meeting on turf
  replacement rebates.

VIII.  COMPOSTING ACTIVITIES

  Staff provided an update to the Commission on the Community Gardens managed by
  the Parks and Recreation Department and confirmed there is a manager for the site.
  There is a 10-year waiting list and currently there is no composting at the site. The
  site is inspected every Sunday to ensure the plots are being properly maintained.
  There are a total of 90 plots at the site. Since the City of Alhambra is built out, we
  are not sure where an alternative location can be utilized for composting.
  Commissioner Massaro said there is a Community Garden in El Sereno and everyone
  has their own key. Staff mentioned a composting event will take place again this year
  October 8, 2022 at Granada Park in conjunction with a recycling event; paint drop-off
  and paper shredding. Residents must bring their own containers to pick up the
  compost. Commissioner Vuong inquired about requesting to increase the frequency
  of compost pickup. The event is organized through the City Manager’s Office.
  Commissioner Chan also asked how many people actually participated.
  Commissioner Chan thinks compost should be available to the residents more
  frequently for residents that are ECO friendly. The flyers will be sent to the
  Commission and they will be posted on the City’s website. Massaro asked if the
  event needed volunteers as she would like to volunteer. Staff will obtain additional
  information regarding the attendance and volunteering opportunities.

 IX.  CITY OF ALHAMBRA TREE ORDINANCE

  Commissioner Chan suggested to amend AMC Chapter 23.88 Section D (1) No
  replacement tree required for the removal of a diseased or hazardous. Commissioner
  Chan thinks there should be a requirement to replace the tree to provide shade to our
  residents and animals. In general, we need to have more trees and this is the right
  step going forward. Trees should be replaced with California native trees. Staff did
  not know why this was included in the ordinance. This is alarming to Commissioner
  Chan. Staff suggested to do research on why this was included and review other tree
  ordinances in neighboring cities. Commissioner Vuong suggested we get feedback
  from our Tree Maintenance Administrative Aide. Also, look for public lands to have
  tree planting events throughout the City. Community engagement is important to get
  more residents involved so they can be aware of the environment. Staff will conduct
  research to see if we have any tree planting events in the works and see if grants are
  available. The ECO Fair may be an option to share information regarding tree
  planting.

  X.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Staff mentioned two items to add to the next agenda; 1) Updates for the Sustainability
  Plan and the Tree Ordinance. Commissioner Massaro suggested the language in the
  Municipal Code should be clear, easy to read and understandable so residents will not
  find it difficult to comply with the regulations.

  Page 4 of 5
 Commissioner Vuong will not be available for meetings until after December 2022.
Commissioner Chan motioned to adjourn the meeting at 19:13, Commissioner Vuong
seconded. Motion unanimously approved. Meeting adjourned at 19:14.

   ITEM #3

Environmental Sustainability Commission Meeting- November 10, 2022
Update Items

  1. Sustainability Plan

  The City has received the funding agreement documents from HUD and will go to Council to
  approve a solicitation to release a Request for Proposal to develop the Sustainability Plan.

  2. Tree Ordinance

  The City does replace diseased or hazardous trees in the public right-of way. The property
  owner must agree to maintain the tree. The City replaces approximately 75 trees every year.

  For private property, the reason why there is no requirement to replace a diseased or hazardous
  tree is to not place an undue hardship on a property owner to replace the tree. It is the City’s
  understanding that it is not the fault of the owner and often times a tree has reached its
  maximum life span.

  3. Turf Replacement Rebate

  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) is interested in applying for the DWR
  Drought Relief Grant to provide assistance to its member agencies to fund a turf replacement
  rebate program. The City of Alhambra has expressed interest and provided feedback to the
  SGVMWD.

§ 23.48.010 PURPOSE.

  (A) Landscaping should be designed using elements pertaining to the form, horizontal and vertical lines, hardscape and
softscape, and ornate qualities that are compatible with the primary structure. Visual openness and water efficiency shall be
maintained. Special attention shall be given to selecting appropriate trees and plants that, at their maturity, will be in scale
with the structure(s).
 (B) To conform to the state mandated Model Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance as required by Government Code
Section 65595 and as published at the Title 23, California Code of Regulations 490 et seq.
(‘86 Code, § 23.48.010) (Ord. 4110, passed - - ; Am. Ord. 4552, passed 11-23-09; Am. Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.020 DEFINITIONS.

  For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
  ARTIFICIAL TURF. A synthetically derived, natural grass substitute that may be used in lieu of natural turf, and must
simulate the appearance of natural live grass, in a single-family residence and in the landscape areas of multi-family and
non-residential properties. To be used, ARTIFICIAL TURF must meet minimum standards for materials, installation and
maintenance.
  (1) MATERIALS. Artificial turf must have a minimum eight-year no-fade warranty as issued by the manufacturer; be
cut-pile infill, minimum pile height one and two-thirds inches and a maximum of one and three-quarter inches, with parallel
long slit blades;
  (a) The synthetic turf blades (not including the thatch layer) shall be required to contain at least two natural green
colors.
  (b) The turf must contain a beige or tan thatch layer.
  (c) Be affixed to a permeable triple-layer backing and allow water to percolate through the synthetic grass at a drain
rate of at least 30 inches per hour, to an adequate drainage system installed underneath the artificial turf to prevent run-off,
pooling and flooding.
  (d) The synthetic turf shall comply with all federal and state standards related to lead and heavy metal content.
  (e) The fill material shall be of silica sand or zeolite material that is brushed in to keep the blades upright and achieve
a natural grass look. Any replacement fill shall be the same. The use of rubber crumb infill is prohibited.
  (f) Must be constructed to maximize dimensional stability, resist damage during normal use and minimize UV
degradation with a tear grab strength of at least 200 pounds. It must be resistant to staining, weather, insects, rot, mildew,
and fungus and shall be non-allergenic and non-toxic and able to pass the pill burn test for flammability.
  (g) The use of indoor/outdoor carpeting, and artificial shrubs, flowers, tress, and vines instead of natural plantings is
prohibited.
  (2) INSTALLATION. Artificial turf must be installed pursuant to manufacturers requirements by a licensed professional
with experience in the installation of artificial turf. In addition:
  (a) Installation must include removal of all existing plant material and three inches of a compacted aggregate base
that provides adequate drainage and ensure stability.
  (b) The area must be sloped and graded to prevent excessive pooling, runoff, or flooding onto adjacent property.
Artificial turf areas must be sufficiently drained to live planting areas to provide complete infiltration of runoff.
   ITEM
  (c) Artificial turf must be permanently anchored over the entire coverage area with nails and glue, and  #6
  all seams must
be nailed, or sewn and glued so as to conceal the edges, with the grain pointing a single direction.
  (d) All existing irrigation infrastructure in the covered area, including piping and sprinkler heads that are no longer
used must be capped or removed and shall not be visible.
  (e) Artificial turf must be separated from live planting areas by a barrier such as a mow strip or bender board to
prevent mixing of natural plant materials and artificial turf.
  (f) All efforts shall be made to protect existing trees and tree roots from damage during installation.
  (g) Artificial turf may not be installed within a five-foot diameter of the trunk of any landscape tree.
  (h) Artificial turf is prohibited in all parkways.
  (3) MAINTENANCE. Artificial turf must be maintained in an attractive and clean, unfaded condition free of weeds,
stains, debris, tears, holes, depressions, ruts, odors and looseness at edges and seams. Damaged or worn areas in the
artificial turf surface must be repaired or removed and replaced in a manner that results in consistent appearance with the
existing artificial turf. The artificial turf surface must be replaced once it is unable to be maintained as required. Vehicle
parking on artificial turf is prohibited.
  AUTOMATIC IRRIGATION SYSTEM. All landscaped areas shall be provided with an AUTOMATIC IRRIGATION
SYSTEM capable of complete coverage of the landscaped areas (head-to-head coverage). Water conservation techniques
shall be incorporated into the design of the IRRIGATION SYSTEM and shall be designed to minimize run-off and other
wasting of water. Projects are encouraged to incorporate gray water collection and reuse systems
  DECORATIVE HARDSCAPE. Materials used to enhance the landscape area which includes but are not limited to material
such as cobble rock, decomposed granite in combination with binding material, brickwork, gravel, pavers, fountains,
stamped concrete and pavers.
 DRIP IRRIGATION. Any low volume irrigation system utilizing emission devices with a flow rate equal to or less than two
gallons per hour.
  DROUGHT TOLERANT LANDSCAPING. A variety of native plants and landscaping alternatives, including the installation
of synthetic grass or artificial turf.
  FRONT SETBACK. The distance between the public street right-of-way line and the front line of a building or any
projection thereof, excluding uncovered steps.
  HARDSCAPES. Any durable material or feature (pervious and non-pervious) installed in or around a landscaped area,
such as pavements or walls.
  LANDSCAPE PLANS. Refers to the planting, irrigation and hardscape plans designed and prepared by a landscape
designer or a landscape architect, who indicates the type, size and location of vegetative and accent material proposed for
the landscaping of a site including all irrigation and other devices necessary to maintain such landscaping.
  NON-PERVIOUS. Any surface or natural material that does not allow for the passage of water through the material and
into the underlying soil.
  PARKWAY. A portion of a street right-of-way, between the back of the curb line and the lot line, which is used or is
available for use for landscaping, utilities and/or sidewalks.
 PERVIOUS. Any surface or material that allows the passage of water through the material and into the underlying soil.
 TURF. A ground cover surface of mowed grass. Annual bluegrass, Kentucky bluegrass, Perennial ryegrass. Red fescue,
and Tall fescue are cool-season grasses. Bermuda grass, Kikuyu grass, Seashore Paspalum, St. Augustine grass.
Zoysiagrass, and Buffalo grass are warm-season grasses.
(Ord. 4552, passed 11-23-09; Am. Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.030 APPLICABILITY OF STATE MODEL WATER EFFICIENT LANDSCAPE ORDINANCE.

  All projects that require landscape and irrigation plan review as required by the Model Water Efficient Landscape
Ordinance shall comply with 23 California Code of Regulations 490, et seq. Applicants for such projects shall submit
landscape and irrigation plans compliant with the Model Water Efficiency Landscape Ordinance for approval by the Design
Review Board.
(Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.040 LANDSCAPING REQUIREMENTS FOR RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL PROPERTIES.

 All residential and commercial landscaping abutting a public or private street which are not otherwise subject to §
23.48.030 are still required to comply with the following sections of this chapter: §§23.48.050, 23.48.070 and 23.48.080.
(‘86 Code, §§ 9.70.020, 23.48.020) (Ord. 4110, passed - - ; Am. Ord. 4152, passed - - ; Am. Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.050 ACCEPTABLE GROUND COVER REQUIREMENTS.
   (A) Residential. Drought tolerant landscape materials shall be the primary materials used. No more thanITEM  #6the front
  25% of
yard setback area shall be covered by non-decorative hardscape features (e.g., concrete, asphalt, gravel, driveways,
sidewalks, etc.) No more than 25% may be covered by decorative permeable hardscape features (e.g., brick, stone, mulch,
water feature, etc.). The remaining 50% front yard setback area, must be of drought tolerant landscape material and an
automatic irrigation system shall be required for the front and street side yard landscape area(s). In the event that the
original driveway exceeds 50% of the front yard setback, no additional hardscape shall be permitted.
  (1) With the exception of slopes of three feet or greater vertical height (which shall be planted and irrigated with an
automatic irrigation system), rear yard areas, and side yard areas located behind a wall or solid fence, are not required to be
landscaped.
  (B) Parkways. Live plant materials shall be the primary materials used. No more than 25% of the parkway area shall be
covered by non-decorative hardscape features (e.g., concrete, asphalt, gravel, sidewalks, etc.) No more than 25% may be
covered by decorative permeable hardscape features (e.g., brick, mulch, etc.). The remaining 50% of the parkway area must
be of live plant material which shall not exceed 36 inches in height and an automatic irrigation system shall be required for
the parkway area(s). Loose decorative stone and sharp or thorned plant material are discouraged. Artificial turf is not
allowed in parkways.
  (C) Commercial. If a setback fronting on a public right-of-way (excluding alley ways) exists, no more than 75% of the
setback area shall be covered by hardscape features (e.g. concrete, asphalt, gravel, driveways, sidewalks, etc.) The
remaining 25% must be drought tolerant landscape material and an automatic irrigation system shall be required.
(‘86 Code, § 9.70.030) (Ord. 4152, passed - - ; Am. Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.060 LANDSCAPE PLANS.

  (A) Plans and specifications for landscaping, irrigation systems, tree preservation and slope planting for erosion control
shall reflect use of the following:
  (1) Planting materials of a type, size and placement compatible with the project and surrounding land uses;
  (2) Sound soil-preparation and planting practices.
 (B) All landscape plans that are submitted to the city shall include the following:
  (1) For new multiple-family residential developments:
  (a) A minimum of one different plant type per 1,000 square feet of lot area shall be provided, up to a maximum of ten
different plant types;
  (b) A minimum of one 24-inch box tree per 50 feet of street frontage(s) shall be provided. The box trees shall be
located in the yard(s) that front upon a street;
  (2) The plant materials incorporated into the plan shall be of the type that are well-suited to the city’s climate zone;
  (3) The plant materials incorporated into the plan are encouraged to be drought-tolerant;
  (4) Residential projects shall have a diversity of plant material incorporated into the plan.
  (5) On all multiple-family residential projects, landscaping shall be installed at the driveway level between the garages.
Such landscaping shall not interfere with the required turning radius.
 (C) All landscaped areas shall be served by a permanent automatic irrigation system such as the following:
  (1) Automatic controllers. Automatic control systems shall be required for all irrigation systems and shall be able to
accommodate all aspects of the design.
  (2) Drip irrigation/xerigation. The use of drip irrigation shall be considered whenever appropriate.
  (3) Plant groupings. Plants that require different amounts of water shall be irrigated by separate valves. If one valve is
used for a given area, only plants with similar water use shall be used in that area. Anti-drain (check) valves shall be
installed at strategic points to prevent low-head drainage.
  (4) Sprinkler heads. Heads and emitters shall have consistent application rates within each control valve circuit.
Sprinkler heads shall be selected for proper area coverage, application rate, operating pressure, adjustment capability, and
ease of maintenance.
  (5) Rain-sensing devices. Rain sensing override devices shall be required for any project with a landscaped area

  (6) Moisture-sensing devices. Soil moisture sensing devices shall be required for any project with a landscaped area
greater than 10,000 square feet.
  (D) All landscaping and planter areas shall be installed consistent with the approved landscaping plan, prior to the permit

§ 23.48.070 UNACCEPTABLE GROUND COVER.

  Concrete, asphalt, or similar materials, or any other solid, continuous covering is not an acceptable ground cover. Bare dirt
front yards and street side yards are strictly prohibited under the provisions of this chapter.
(‘86 Code, § 9.70.040) (Ord. 4152, passed - - ; Am. Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.080 MAINTENANCE.

  Landscape abutting streets must be maintained in such a way as to keep all plant life alive, thriving and displaying its
natural colors and shall be properly trimmed and cut. Inert matter, such as, gravel, decorative stone, or other acceptable
ground covers not consisting of live vegetation, shall be kept neat, well-ordered and clear of the public right of way.
Overgrown weeds, dead or dying plant material shall be replaced.
(‘86 Code, § 9.70.050) (Ord. 4152, passed - - ; Am. Ord. 4682, passed 1-11-16)
§ 23.48.090 PENALTY.

  Notwithstanding any other provision of the Alhambra Municipal Code to the contrary, any person who causes, permits,
suffers, or maintains a public nuisance, or any person who violates any provision of this chapter, or who fails to comply with
any obligation or requirement of this chapter, is in violation of the Alhambra Municipal Code.
